summary: Extensions should stage write-back behind policy, analyze drift in batches, and preserve the rationale for accepting or rejecting reconciliation.

items.text: Use risk-tiered write-back: low-risk formatting may auto-merge after checks, semantic changes become pull requests, and privileged or destructive updates require explicit approval.
Generate a periodic drift report that clusters duplicate mismatches, estimates blast radius, and assigns owners before opening individual changes.
Store accepted, rejected, deferred, and superseded reconciliation decisions with evidence so the next cycle does not repeatedly reopen intentional differences.
Require contract, schema, link-integrity, and generation-idempotence checks before a write-back can update an authoritative artifact.
